# Recording B structural locality: preregistration proposal

**Status: PROPOSAL ONLY; primary review required before tooling or collection.** This document freezes a proposed question and finite design, not executable protocol acceptance. Dense Recording A ended `UNRESOLVED`, and the locked dense owner-kernel qualification remains FAIL. Recording B is an independent structural product gate. No dense attribution, physical container, compiler/runtime optimization, or React speed claim follows from it.

## Question, source basis, and eligible semantics

For a compiler-authored keyed list, does one local edit still cause work proportional to all `N` rows? Separate **owner discovery/component execution** from **sequence/index/binding/token maintenance** and required host/lifecycle work. `N` means live keyed rows before an edit; `K` means changed keys. A local path should keep owner/component work bounded by `K` plus fixed ancestor depth and keep sequence repair bounded by touched buckets/keys; an `N/2` filter is intentionally global. Ratios and counters are reported at every size, not inferred from one large result.

The proposed native authored syntax is the checked-in `createKeyedCollection` + direct `rows.map((row) => <Row key={row.id} ... />)` pattern in `src/browser/native_product_mixed_arm.tsx`, compiled by the actual Rust/OXC Vite native module. The public collection API supports versioned `insert`, `remove`, `move`, `replace` batches and falls back to a snapshot when a reader expires. `renderCollectionAt` takes the initial snapshot and later can consume delta batches; `ComponentStateRoot.#flushCollectionDelta` prepares affected rows and calls `VDOMSnapshotRoot.commitKeyedRegionDelta`. This path requires one keyed component site and an eligible single host root with no nested component/store read, `requiresOwnerRender`, compiled graph/column bindings, or incompatible scalar binding groups. These are source-observed guards, **not a promise that every TSX map is sparse**. Count actual path selection and every bail reason. The existing product-mixed controller updates three scalar states in every retained row and may flush twice; its timings cannot isolate structural locality. Its edit helper also builds a whole-list `Set`/`filter`/`slice` target outside the collection API.

Build one new structural-only paired fixture from authored TSX, preserving the same keyed `li` output, native row local state/effect and React row local state/layout effect. Native creates a keyed collection and invokes `collection.apply(version, operations); root.flush()`; React owns an `ids` state array and invokes a precomputed `setIds(nextIds)` inside `flushSync`. The React fixture must be verified to pass through `babel-plugin-react-compiler` in Vite; `vite.config.ts` currently lists the older structural benchmark but does **not** list `product_mixed_react_arm.tsx`. The first executable gate must compile the actual **stateful, effectful authored row** and prove the emitted collection site, state/effect sites, transformed row, React memo-cache sites, served assets, and runtime delta path. Row state, sentinel effects or a compiler-emitted direct column may make the VDOM delta ineligible; that result is recorded, not repaired by removing state or hand-writing generated bindings. Include a deliberately unsupported/bail fixture with explicit diagnostic or generic-fallback correctness evidence. Record every compiler diagnostic and reject a latency page with an unproved transform or silent fallback. Source hashes and served asset hashes are fixed before collection.

The older `component_state_structural_benchmark.tsx` and `compiler/fixtures/component_state_structural.tsx` form a **separate old state-array basis**, with a generated transform checked in, three operations, programmatic click plus microtask settle, and diagnostic counters. It is a useful semantic/counter precedent, not a matched latency baseline. The current VDOM source includes the live adjacent-token patch (`cdc774...`), whereas the archived qualified dense build used `00d851...`; Recording B locks the **live** source explicitly and never inherits dense qualification. `KeyedRegionBuckets` counters already cover slot reads/writes, split/merge; linked collection stats cover inspections. Neither proves integrated latency or owner locality alone.

Eligible authored cases: direct collection binding, one inline synchronous one-parameter arrow map returning keyed JSX, stable unique string keys, one row component site, single host row, collection operations with valid anchors/version, ordinary scalar props and native local state/effect. The Rust compiler explicitly diagnoses aliased collection map, invalid callback, index parameter or `thisArg`; ordinary arrays remain generic. Collection reads outside the map may require owner render. Dynamic/nested row components, store/resource readers, compiled CSR/column bindings, stale reader, invalid keys/anchors, and host-region ambiguity must use their documented generic path or fail explicitly. The generic oracle is a separately compiled native state-array list with the same visible contract; it may cost `Θ(N)` and must remain correct. Do not label unsupported syntax as an optimized success. Global filter uses a predeclared batch of `N/2` public remove operations on the eligible collection, and the state-array oracle/React receive the corresponding filtered array; it is not evidence for local complexity.

## Frozen finite matrix and intervals

Sizes: **128, 1,024, 10,000** rows, matching prior structural and current qualified scale and giving an 78-fold range to distinguish a constant/local count from a linear visit count. One canonical ordered list `row-0…row-(N-1)` per trial; unique inserted keys include page/block/trial ID. Exactly **12 edit kinds**:

| Kind | One timed edit from canonical list | Expected structural scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| insert head/middle/tail | insert one new key before `row-0`, `row-floor(N/2)`, or end | one new owner and host row |
| remove head/middle/tail | remove `row-0`, `row-floor(N/2)`, or `row-(N-1)` | one retired owner/host row |
| move to head/middle/tail | move tail→head, head→middle, or head→tail with one `move` | one retained owner and host placement |
| same-key rotation | move `row-0` to end, preserving every key | one retained owner and placement |
| edge replacement | remove last key and insert one new key at head, one public batch | two owner lifetimes, two host changes |
| global filter | remove odd keys in one public batch | `N/2` retirements; broad control |

For each timed edit, first restore the canonical list and sentinel row state in an **untimed reset**; verify reset identity/lifecycle and wait for all scheduled work to settle before timing. No inverse edit or DOM inspection enters the edit interval. The 10,000 filter is budgeted as one broad operation per trial; if a page exceeds 90 seconds, mark that page invalid and stop that size, without silently dropping the filter or reducing replication. The fixtures use identical displayed output and keys; differences in authored native delta API versus React array state are explicit and reported. Prepare immutable operation descriptors and `nextIds` outside the clock. Native timed interval starts immediately before public `apply` and ends after synchronous `root.flush`; React starts immediately before `flushSync(() => setIds(nextIds))` and ends on its return. Include version checks, setters, scheduling and host commit in each arm's public operation. Report separately the untimed input construction, cold compiler/build, fresh mount, reset, retained memory, and teardown/disposal. No RAF/paint/presentation claim. Do not use per-cell timers or render-time React counters.

Exactly **five paired blocks per size**, each block two fresh pages (native, React), alternating AB/BA orders. Proposed seed `0x5b2026`; proposed size order is `128, 1024, 10000`; pair indexes are `0…4`. At 128 and 10,000, arm order is `native/react` for even pair indexes and `react/native` for odd indexes; reverse this at 1,024. Within a page, operation order is the table order rotated left by `(sizeIndex + pairIndex + trialIndex) mod 12`, then reversed for odd trial indexes; both arm pages of a block use the same order and unique key tokens. This gives the closest possible AB/BA balance with five pairs per size (3/2 or 2/3); report order effects. These values remain **proposed** until executable preregistration fixes the source/build/collector and schedule hashes; do not adapt them after seeing timings. Each page runs the 12 operations, **two warmup plus eight measured trials per operation**, or 120 edit trials/page plus resets. Every trial returns to canonical order outside the timed interval. Thus 30 latency pages total, 8 measured samples per operation/page, and five independent paired page blocks per size; serial trials are not independent experimental units. Give a 90-second headless, GPU-disabled, interruptible cap **per page**, with Portless HTTPS preview and owned cleanup under `$portless-dev-servers`. The 120-trial page is a budget proposal, not a demonstrated 90-second fit: a staged build/output/one-page collector-protocol gate must establish compiler proof, semantics and deadline before approving the full matrix. If 10,000 cannot fit, stop and report incomplete preregistered evidence rather than adapt sample counts or drop an operation after observation. For each operation/size report page median and p95 descriptively; with eight samples, within-page p95 is effectively the maximum and **cannot qualify a tail claim**. Report five paired page-level ratios/differences and their range, with no frame-level confidence claim. A second device is required before a broad product performance claim, outside this bounded first recording.

Count controls are separate fresh native pages with the same 12-operation schedule, one page/size, no timing interpretation. Count effective placements separately from no-op `place` calls. Record `K`, live `N`, resulting size, host output count, and exact path ID. The counter window opens after canonical reset and closes at synchronous commit return; diagnostics, DOM inspection, `collection.snapshot()`, and the next reset are outside it. `KeyedCollection.stats()` is cumulative, so take before/after deltas or `resetStats()` only at this boundary. Its `entryInspections` includes `snapshot()` traversal and `map()` fallback; an `N` count during mount/reset/inspection must be charged there, not to the edit. Similarly, `VDOMSnapshotRoot.snapshot` serializes mounted nodes when dirty, so do not call it inside the count window. `collection.rows-prepared` counts prepared inserted/replaced rows, not all owner visits. React output/identity/lifecycle is checked without a render counter in qualified latency pages; optional React diagnostics require a separate build/page and are never used for latency comparison.

| Obligation and current source anchor | Existing counter scope | Missing seam for count control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Collection preflight and snapshot: `src/keyed_collection.ts:135`, `:197–245`, `:458–473`; compiler initial `renderCollectionAt` snapshot: `src/component_state_runtime.ts:663–668` | `entryInspections`, `anchorInspections`, listener/reader stats are cumulative; snapshot deliberately walks all entries | Attribute each before/after delta to edit versus reset/mount/fallback; count snapshot invocations and rows only inside runtime edit |
| Root route and collection delta: `src/component_state_runtime.ts:1940–1990`, `:4075–4110`, `:4501` | delta operations, reader-expired, stale/render fallback; `profileCounter` emitted at flush end | one exclusive path ID per edit; reader batches and exact bail/guard reason, generic full render entry |
| Row/owner work: `src/component_state_runtime.ts:4140–4225`, `:4390–4465`, `:4511–4532`, generic expansion `:5692–5735` | `owner.component-visits/renders`, `owner.created/retired`, `collection.rows-prepared`, ancestor membership writes | owner lookup and lineage visits, row component executions by path, state/effect activation/cleanup counts; distinguish one row from all-owner rediscovery |
| VDOM delta and fallback: `src/vdom_snapshot_runtime.ts:1375–1422`, `:1501–1568`, full key rebuild `:4658–4662` | delta bail labels, binding attach/detach/index operations, full key rebuild visits, partial commit count | full reconcile mounted-node visits, normalized candidate subtree visits, token rebuilds, exclusive fallback reason |
| Bucket order: `src/keyed_region_buckets.ts:93–165`, `:177–191`, `:235–269` | cumulative slot reads/writes, splits/merges, bucket count | expose per-edit before/after stats through diagnostic seam; count key/rank/offset repairs, not just operations |
| Binding/host/lifetime: `src/vdom_snapshot_runtime.ts:1501–1548`, `:4003–4080`, `:485–500`; old counting host `src/browser/component_state_structural_benchmark.tsx:60–115` | VDOM binding index operations and old host insert/move/remove/prop calls | separate effective/no-op host placement, disposal and effect cleanup; include custom host resource disposal where applicable |

Before and after each edit, each page compares ordered DOM signature, text/attributes and local state against the deterministic expected model; the collector matches native and React signatures for the same block/trial across separate pages. Hold DOM references and row state for retained keys **within that edit**; moved/rotated keys keep identity and selected state without effect cleanup/remount. Removal retires the old node/owner and invokes one cleanup; insertion gets a fresh identity and one mount. A reset can reinsert the same textual key with a **new incarnation** and must not be treated as continuity from the pre-removal edit. Inserted rows use unique IDs/tokens. Before every edit, mark fixed sentinel `row-2` selected (retained by all 12 operations) and, for moves/rotation, mark the moving key selected too; establish these state updates before the clock. Native `useEffect` activation/cleanup and React `useLayoutEffect` registration/cleanup have different scheduling, so compare settled mount/cleanup cardinality and observable output, not effect timing. Native dead setters may reject after retirement while React setters may be ignored; record each arm's documented behavior and never require identical throw behavior. Check listener/ref/resource disposal where used, and final empty root. A separately compiled generic native oracle gets **three fresh pages, one per size**, with the full operation schedule and correctness/lifetime traces but no latency inclusion; that is the maximum oracle page budget. Initial/final snapshots, reset construction and inspection may be `Θ(N)` and stay outside timed/count edit windows; record their own work. Correctness failure invalidates the page.

## Stop, interpretation, and dependency order

Preregistered descriptive locality screen: for each one-key edit, owner/component visit counts at 10,000 must be no more than the 1,024 count plus **16 fixed ancestor/guard visits** and no more than **64 total**; any count above `N/4` at either 1,024 or 10,000 is a clear full-region failure. Intermediate counts are `UNRESOLVED`, not renamed local. Report all three `N` values and normalized visits/`N`, plus sequence/index/binding/token and host counts. For global filter, proportional work is expected and excluded from the local screen. These thresholds are diagnostic operational definitions, not a proof of asymptotic complexity from three points.

If any eligible local edit triggers `Θ(N)` owner discovery or component execution, stop at **upstream rediscovery**; review a source-mapped way to retire that work before considering a sequence container. If owner work passes but sequence/index/binding/token repair grows materially with `N`, isolate its count and matched latency cost first; only then compare current indexed array versus existing bounded buckets under a separate accepted protocol. If host placements/disposals or necessary global work dominate, report that floor. A B+ tree, SoA conversion or new registry is not authorized by this recording. If correctness, compiler provenance, source/asset lock, timing semantics, 90-second cap, or page completeness fails, stop affected collection and preserve failure receipts; no favorable repeats. No design choice comes from container-only microbenchmarks.

Next implementation order after primary accepts this proposal: (1) source-lock and compiler eligibility proof for authored **stateful** native/generic/React fixtures, with diagnostics, emitted plans/assets and an unsupported/bail correctness case; (2) shared operation schedule and DOM/lifecycle oracle within the three-page oracle budget; (3) separate count instrumentation at the identified seams, with no React render probes in latency build; (4) finite collector/analyzer, synthetic receipt checks and **one bounded page protocol gate** before the full matrix; (5) Luna runs paired pages and count controls only after primary accepts that gate; (6) independent primary review of source/served locks, page-level analysis and cleanup. Owners: Sol 6 Medium implements tooling in disjoint fixture/compiler, runtime-counter, collector/analyzer files after review; Luna alone runs tests/build/bench/Portless browser; primary reviews and integrates. No production physical optimization is part of this sequence.
